simple.meaning: דֹּחַן (dôchan) is a Hebrew object word meaning “millet.” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Ezekiel 4:9. The background is built from the passages where the word occurs.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to דֹּחַן (H1764) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.

definitions.full: H1764. dochan דֹּ֫חַן noun masculine millet (Late Hebrew דּוֺחַן , Aramaic ׳ד דּוֺחִינָא ), Ezek 4:9 in the series ׳וְד וְכֻסְּמִים וַעֲדָשִׁים וּפוֺל וּשְׂעֹרִים חִטִּין see Löw 72 .

occurrences.englishText: “Take for yourself also wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt, and put them in one vessel. Make bread of it. According to the number of the days that you will lie on your side, even three hundred ninety days, you shall eat of it.
